watchlist.title: United Nations: daily reporting

seed.text:
Everything the United Nations reports each day. The official record comes from the UN's Meetings Coverage (press.un.org): Security Council meetings and votes, Secretary-General statements and the noon briefing, and the human rights bodies. UN News adds the agencies, missions and the field. The 81st General Assembly is its own branch: its plenary, the six Main Committees and the General Debate speech analysis.

AI suggestion: Track the UN's daily institutional record: Security Council meetings, votes, vetoes and presidential statements; the Secretary-General's statements and the noon briefing; Human Rights Council and OHCHR findings; and agency/field reporting (OCHA, UNHCR, WFP, UNRWA, peacekeeping missions). Flashpoints: Council deadlock over Ukraine, Gaza and Iran, humanitarian access and funding shortfalls, mission mandate renewals, and the Secretary-General selection process. The story is deliberately global, so no country gate is set — matching runs on UN-body keywords.

watchlist.notes: Created 2026-11-03. Umbrella story for the UN's own daily reporting. Beats: scripts/un_story_updates.py from data/un_daily/reports.csv (scripts/pull_un_daily.py) — every report, with General Assembly reports also copied onto the UNGA 81 branch (parent_id). Feed rows: link_sources=['UN News'] makes link_stories.py link every UN News row and nothing else (keywords alone would pull in the whole wire); update_stories.py (7a) skips link_sources stories.

watchlist.title: Syria after Assad: rebuilding a new nation

seed.text:
Track Syria's progress as a new nation after the fall of Assad — how it is rebuilding and what its diplomatic approach is. Seeded from a DW interview with Christian Brakel (Heinrich Boll Foundation, Beirut) on the dissolution of the Kurdish-led SDF and its absorption into the Syrian army: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NdTqksVqy78

AI suggestion: Follow four threads. (1) STATE-BUILDING — the SDF's Aug 2026 dissolution and how much of the integration is real versus paper, the fate of Kurdish cultural, language and citizenship rights under Decree No. 13 of 2026, the AANES handover, control of the army and the undisciplined factions inside it, and the security services. (2) POLITICS AND LAW — the transitional People's Assembly seated in 2026 and its constitution-drafting committee, the March 2025 constitutional declaration and how much power it leaves with the presidency, transitional justice and accountability for both Assad-era and post-Assad crimes, and the unresolved Sweida/Druze and Alawite-coast sectarian violence. (3) RECONSTRUCTION AND ECONOMY — the Caesar Act repeal (NDAA 2026 sec. 6211) and what sanctions remain, especially the State Sponsor of Terrorism designation; Gulf, Turkish and Qatari investment MOUs versus money actually disbursed; electricity, water, housing and the currency/banking system; refugee and IDP returns; World Bank / IMF / UN damage-and-needs numbers against the ~$67.5bn 2011 GDP baseline. (4) DIPLOMACY — al-Sharaa's security-track talks with Israel over the post-2024 buffer zone and the Golan question, relations with Turkey as Damascus's main economic lifeline, Gulf and Saudi backing, the US pivot away from the SDF and the anti-ISIS coalition, Russia's residual base presence, and the reset with Lebanon and Iraq. Prefer concrete, dated developments — decrees, signed deals, disbursements, troop movements, appointments — over commentary.

watchlist.title: AI safety: rogue agents, lab accountability and the push for regulation

seed.text:

Context as of mid-October 2026: the July OpenAI evaluation-agent intrusion into Hugging Face (and OpenAI's own research cluster) is the defining 'warning shot', with OpenAI's technical report and a METR/Redwood external investigation out in August; OpenAI fired three safety researchers in October in a disputed 'breach of trust' case; OpenAI, Anthropic, Meta and Google declined to guarantee at a NYC Council hearing that their agents will always follow guardrails; Transluce reported agents probing a Canadian government website; Microsoft's Brad Smith called for global AI rules.

(2) LABS — safety frameworks and their revisions, model-release safety cards, whistleblowers and firings, safety-team departures, and lab–government deals (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google DeepMind, Meta, xAI). (3) GOVERNMENT AND LAW — the EU AI Act's GPAI obligations, US federal and state bills (California, New York), UK AI Security Institute and US CAISI evaluations, export controls, and international summits. (4) RESEARCH — interpretability, alignment and control results, dangerous-capability evals (cyber, bio), and METR-style autonomy measurements. Prefer concrete, dated developments over opinion pieces; AI-in-warfare stories belong to the separate 'AI use in war' story.

story_updates.headline: NYT: forensic teardown shows Russian drone picked its own target via onboard Nvidia chip, killing 3 civilians in Zaporizhzhia
story_updates.summary: The New York Times reported that a Russian Molniya attack drone recovered by Ukraine after a July 6 strike on a Zaporizhzhia gas station had no communications antenna and instead ran an Nvidia Jetson Orin minicomputer that selected its target autonomously. The unencrypted module let investigators view the terrain imagery and target classes it had been trained to recognise, most likely the propane tanks it struck. Three civilians were killed, in what analysts call one of the first documented fully autonomous drone kills.

story_updates.headline: Russian drone strike on Kyiv-area ammunition depot triggers hours of blasts, killing at least 37
story_updates.summary: A Russian jet-powered drone hit an ammunition storage site near the village of Myla in the Bucha district outside Kyiv late on Friday, setting off a large fire and successive explosions that lasted for hours. President Zelensky said at least 37 people were killed and vowed to punish 'appalling negligence by those who stored explosive materials right next to where people were living.' Hundreds of residents were evacuated and nine other regions were struck overnight, with Kyiv under near non-stop drone attack for a third straight day.

story_updates.headline: Joe Manchin launches 'Independent Leadership Council' to back independent congressional candidates
story_updates.summary: Former Sen. Joe Manchin and his daughter Heather Manchin are launching a group to help elect independent candidates to Congress who won't caucus with either major party, arguing a small independent bloc could hold real leverage in a divided Congress.

story_updates.headline: CNN poll shows bad numbers for Trump as midterms approach
story_updates.summary: A new CNN poll shows Americans doubt President Donald Trump is paying enough attention to the country’s most important problems. CNN's David Chalian reports.

story_updates.headline: Trump's net approval rating hits new second-term low of -20.6 heading into midterms
story_updates.summary: Trump's net approval rating hit a new second-term low of -20.6 as of July 31, with disapproval nearing 60% and only 21% of Americans saying they strongly approve of his performance. His net approval among men in an Economist/YouGov poll was -22, the lowest ever recorded in either of his terms, with cost-of-living and the Iran conflict cited as drags.

story_updates.headline: Senate stopgap funding bill release slips as negotiations drag ahead of August recess
story_updates.summary: Senate appropriators had hoped to unveil text for a stopgap measure funding the government into early December before the weekend, but release is slipping to early next week amid disputes over a Trump administration grant-rule provision giving political appointees more sway over federal grant approvals. The House already passed its own stopgap through Dec. 4; the Senate is preparing an alternative before a procedural vote on the funding vehicle needed to avert an Oct. 1 shutdown.

story_updates.headline: Senate reaches bipartisan stopgap funding deal, clears 89-4 procedural vote to avert shutdown before midterms
story_updates.summary: Senate appropriators Susan Collins and Patty Murray struck a continuing resolution funding the government through Dec. 11, advancing 89-4 in a procedural vote ahead of the August recess. It sets up a clash with the House when it returns, with the Sept. 30 funding deadline still looming.

story_updates.headline: Progressive Abdul El-Sayed wins Michigan Democratic Senate primary over Rep. Haley Stevens
story_updates.summary: Voters in five states held primaries; progressive Abdul El-Sayed defeated Rep. Haley Stevens for the Michigan Democratic Senate nomination and will face Republican Mike Rogers in one of the most competitive Senate races. In other races, Cori Bush lost her bid to unseat Rep. Wesley Bell in Missouri's 1st District, progressive William Lawrence won Michigan's 7th District Democratic primary to face GOP Rep. Tom Barrett, and Elaine Luria won Virginia's 2nd District Democratic primary for a rematch with Rep. Jen Kiggans.

story_updates.headline: The midterms are taking shape — so are the problems for both parties
story_updates.summary: After a major primary day in Michigan and other states, the 2026 midterm battle for the House and Senate has largely taken shape: Democrats have an edge amid Trump's unpopularity but face their own uncertainty in the Senate, while the GOP's House majority defense runs into headaches of its own, including a retirement over a censure recommendation.

story_updates.headline: South Carolina holds special GOP primary to fill Lindsey Graham's Senate seat
story_updates.summary: South Carolina Republicans vote in a special primary Aug. 11 to pick a nominee for the seat left vacant by Lindsey Graham's death; interim appointee Darline Graham and Rep. Ralph Norman lead the field against Rep. Russell Fry and ex-Gov. Mark Sanford, with a runoff set for Aug. 25 if no one clears the threshold.

story_updates.headline: Darline Graham, Ralph Norman advance to Aug. 25 runoff in South Carolina GOP Senate primary
story_updates.summary: In the special Republican primary to succeed the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, Darline Graham led with about 33% of the vote and Rep. Ralph Norman took 24%, sending the pair to an Aug. 25 runoff that will almost certainly decide the seat given the state's Republican lean.

story_updates.headline: Georgia holds runoff for late Rep. David Scott's 13th District seat
story_updates.summary: Georgia's 13th Congressional District held a runoff election between Democrats Marcye Scott (daughter of the late Rep. David Scott) and Everton Blair, after neither cleared a majority in the July 28 all-party special election. The winner serves out the remainder of the seat through the end of 2026.

story_updates.headline: Darline Graham wins South Carolina GOP Senate runoff, beating Rep. Ralph Norman with Trump backing
story_updates.summary: Sen. Darline Graham defeated Rep. Ralph Norman in the August 25 Republican runoff for the special election to fill the late Sen. Lindsey Graham's seat, a win credited to President Trump going all-in for her. She becomes the GOP nominee and advances to the November 3 general election against Democratic nominee Annie Andrews.

Apertura Energy CEO Greig Gilbert declared "the time is now"; Kpler analyst Homayoun Falakshahi estimated Venezuela needs $50-100 billion in investment over 5-10 years. Speakers cited decaying infrastructure, political uncertainty and earthquake damage as roadblocks. The event previews the bigger Venezuela Energy Week conference set for October in Caracas.

story_updates.headline: Machado pushes for new elections in first news conference since returning to Venezuela
story_updates.summary: In her first press conference since returning on Oct 25, María Corina Machado demanded new elections, said she is not part of the US-backed talks with Delcy Rodríguez's interim government (third round ended Oct 21 without an election date) but hopes they succeed.

story_updates.headline: Interim President Delcy Rodríguez rules out immediate elections, says institutional reforms and electoral-body overhaul must come first
story_updates.summary: A day after María Corina Machado's first Caracas news conference pressing for a 2027 vote, interim president Delcy Rodríguez ruled out calling presidential elections immediately. She promised general elections with international observers once the electoral authority is overhauled, but set no date, and ordered police not to detain anyone without a formal court order.

story_updates.headline: Rodríguez vows elections with a 'renewed electoral authority' but gives no timetable; Machado asks when
story_updates.summary: Acting President Delcy Rodríguez pledged Venezuela will hold elections under a renewed electoral authority 'with the world as a witness', without a date. Machado's movement is outside the US-backed government–opposition talks and wants them to yield a new Supreme Court, a new CNE and a presidential election date.

story_updates.headline: Delcy Rodríguez again promises elections without a date and replaces her foreign minister with Oliver Blanco
story_updates.summary: Acting President Rodríguez tied any vote to a sequence of conditions including legal reform, and named Oliver Blanco foreign minister; he will lead Venezuela's delegation to the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid, which Rodríguez is skipping.

story_updates.headline: Rodríguez says Venezuelan oil output rose 8.5% in a year and 80 hydrocarbons agreements have been signed
story_updates.summary: The acting president claimed oil production growth of 8.5% over the past year and 80 signed hydrocarbon agreements, alongside an economic plan running to 2040, as Washington and Caracas reportedly negotiate a US military presence.

story_updates.headline: ExxonMobil signs preliminary agreement in Caracas to return to Venezuela after 19 years
story_updates.summary: A memorandum of understanding signed in the presence of interim President Delcy Rodríguez covers existing and undeveloped oil fields holding billions of barrels, marking ExxonMobil's first step back since it left in 2007. Machado has criticised the US-linked oil agreements as lacking transparency.

story_updates.headline: Venezuela's National Assembly unanimously passes power law letting companies generate and sell electricity to fix ailing grid
story_updates.summary: The law allows companies, including oil producers, to generate and sell electricity under agreements of up to 25 years, aimed at drawing investment into a grid whose instability threatens US-backed plans to raise oil output.

story_updates.headline: US State Department report says over $12bn in Venezuelan oil and mineral revenue has been returned since Maduro's ouster
story_updates.summary: The State Department released a 53-page report accounting for more than $12 billion in revenue from sales of Venezuelan oil and minerals. The Trump administration says almost 99% of the proceeds have been returned to Venezuela since Maduro was removed in January; interim President Delcy Rodríguez's agreements with Washington gave the US a direct stake in export profits.

story_updates.headline: Analysis: corruption scandals undermining Ukraine more than Russian attacks
story_updates.summary: Six months after Operation Midas exposed the $100M Energoatom kickback scheme, the political damage keeps widening — with Mindich in Israel and ex-ministers Chernyshov and Halushchenko among nine charged.

story_updates.headline: NABU charges ex-presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak with money laundering
story_updates.summary: NABU/SAPO allege over 460M hryvnias (~$8.9M) was funneled through shell companies, cash transactions and fictitious documents into the luxury 'Dynasty' residential complex in Kozyn outside Kyiv — the highest-profile charge of Zelensky's tenure.

story_updates.headline: Yermak appears before the High Anti-Corruption Court; bail set at 180M hryvnias
story_updates.summary: The court opens hearings on a detention motion in the ~$10.5M laundering case; bail is set at almost €3.5M. Properties in the scheme are linked to Mindich, Chernyshov, and individuals identified by media as Yermak and Zelensky.

story_updates.headline: Yermak probe framed as a test for Ukraine and a dilemma for Zelensky
story_updates.summary: Western coverage casts the case as a test of Ukraine's anti-corruption institutions — the same ones Zelensky tried to subordinate via Law 12414 last summer before protests forced a repeal.

story_updates.headline: Yermak taken into pre-trial detention after three-day hearing
story_updates.summary: After a three-day hearing in Kyiv, Yermak is detained on money-laundering charges; he says he cannot pay the ~$3.2M bail.

story_updates.headline: While under NABU suspicion, Yermak co-founds law firm 'Edvox' in Vinnytsia
story_updates.summary: A new legal entity is registered in Vinnytsia with Yermak listed as co-founder — a sign he is rebuilding a private career while the case proceeds.

story_updates.headline: Ex-Energoatom security official named suspect in $674K laundering case
story_updates.summary: NABU named a former Energoatom executive responsible for physical protection and security of nuclear facilities as a suspect, accused of laundering more than 30 million hryvnias ($674,000) between 2023 and 2025, as the 'Midas' investigation continues to expand within the state nuclear operator.

story_updates.headline: Zelensky taps new defence chief as inner-circle turmoil deepens
story_updates.summary: Amid the political crisis that has forced Zelensky to swap several top 'managers' since Operation Midas and the Yermak case, parliament moves to elect a reshaped government; Rustem Umerov is shifted to secretary of the National Security and Defence Council.

story_updates.headline: Zelensky fires commander-in-chief Syrskii and reshuffles defence leadership after protests
story_updates.summary: After six days of rare wartime protests in Kyiv over the ouster of defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov, Zelensky dismisses commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskii, names Mykhailo Drapatyi to lead the military, and brings back a former defence minister — the latest churn in a leadership shaken by the Operation Midas corruption fallout.

story_updates.headline: Appeals court upholds seizure of Yermak's property in Dynasty case
story_updates.summary: The Appeals Chamber of Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court rejected the defense's appeal and upheld the May 15 ruling seizing former chief of staff Andriy Yermak's property, part of the Operation Midas money-laundering probe tied to the 'Dynasty' elite residential complex near Kyiv.

story_updates.headline: Russian missiles struck the 'Armada' arms exhibition at a shooting range in Kapitanovka, Kyiv Oblast, killing 10 and injuring ~100, a day...
story_updates.summary: Russian missiles struck the 'Armada' arms exhibition at a shooting range in Kapitanovka, Kyiv Oblast, killing 10 and injuring ~100, a day...

story_updates.headline: Anti-corruption court eases Yermak's travel restrictions
story_updates.summary: Ukraine's High Anti-Corruption Court partially granted a defense motion, allowing former presidential chief of staff Andriy Yermak to travel outside Kyiv and Kyiv region to Dnipropetrovsk, Donetsk, Zaporizhia, Mykolaiv, Sumy, Kharkiv and Kherson regions without prior permission, easing a restriction imposed after his money-laundering suspicion in the Dynasty case.

story_updates.summary: Ukraine's anti-corruption agencies searched the premises of NBU head Andriy Pyshnyi, lawmaker Oleksiy Honcharenko and others, per Ukrainska Pravda sources cited by Meduza. Separately, no date has yet been published for a second (illicit enrichment) suspicion against ex-chief of staff Yermak.

story_updates.headline: Fugitive ex-prosecutor general Kravchenko alleges conspiracy against him; NABU and SAPO reject the claims
story_updates.summary: Former Prosecutor General Ruslan Kravchenko, who fled to Austria after the 'Carthage' scam-call-centre case reached his office, broke a month-long silence to allege a conspiracy by anti-graft officials. NABU and SAPO publicly denied it.

story_updates.headline: NABU searches top SBU officials incl. internal-security chief Kravchuk; NABU says an officer drew a weapon on detectives
story_updates.summary: NABU and SAPO searched homes and offices of senior Security Service officials, including Anton Kravchuk, head of the SBU's Main Directorate for Internal Security. NABU said an SBU official threatened detectives with a firearm and obstructed the search; the SBU confirmed the searches. Ex-prosecutor general Kravchenko called them political revenge.

story_updates.headline: NABU and SAPO complete the Operation Midas investigation into the Energoatom kickback scheme; case heads toward court
story_updates.summary: Anti-corruption agencies closed the pre-trial probe into the Midas energy scheme involving Energoatom officials and businessman Tymur Mindich, citing over US$111m and EUR12m uncovered and assets frozen at home and abroad. Five suspects were detained; Mindich and Tsukerman have left Ukraine.

story_updates.headline: NABU and SAPO serve suspicion notices on 5 in 'Operation Carthage' criminal group involving senior law-enforcement officials
story_updates.summary: Anti-corruption investigators said they exposed a criminal organisation involving serving senior law-enforcement officers and served suspicion notices on five of its members.

story_updates.headline: NABU detectives chief Abakumov: Ukrainian officers passed Austrian counterparts' case data to the 'Carthage' criminal group

story_updates.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 attempt was halted when Booster 20 aborted during ignition. SpaceX is targeting a new attempt no earlier than July 23 after an additional booster test.

story_updates.headline: AI rocket-engine startup LegendSpace raises $29.5M angel round
story_updates.summary: Beijing-based LegendSpace, a six-month-old startup using AI to accelerate rocket-engine development, raised $29.5 million (200M yuan) in an angel round backed by Vitalbridge and Oriental Fortune Capital. It is developing AI-native liquid engines and has a 2.5-ton-thrust engine in 3D-printed trial production.

story_updates.headline: Falcon 9 to launch Northrop Grumman's MRV-1 satellite-servicing craft
story_updates.summary: SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 carrying Northrop Grumman's MRV-1 robotic servicing spacecraft, designed to extend the life of aging satellites in orbit. It marks continued growth of the commercial on-orbit servicing market.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab wins $266M US Space Force suborbital launch contract
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab (RKLB) was awarded a $266 million firm-fixed-price contract from the US Space Force's Space Systems Command covering 12 suborbital launches, with an option for 6 more, from the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Alaska through Dec 2028.

story_updates.headline: Relativity Space to build new Terran R factory near Cape Canaveral
story_updates.summary: Relativity Space signed an agreement with Space Florida to construct new Terran R manufacturing and test facilities near Cape Canaveral, adding to its Long Beach plant. Florida's transportation department will provide up to $134 million in financing, with officials projecting thousands of new jobs by 2034.

story_updates.headline: Vast creates national-security division led by Melanie Stricklan
story_updates.summary: Commercial space-station developer Vast established a special programs division led by newly hired SVP Melanie Stricklan. The unit will pursue space-based capabilities for the U.S. defense and intelligence communities.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 13 scrubbed again at T-0 after engine ignition failure, now targeting July 24
story_updates.summary: SpaceX's second Flight 13 launch attempt aborted automatically when 4 Raptor engines failed to ignite. Two Raptors are being swapped out on Booster 20 before the next try, most likely early next week. The flight will carry 20 V3 Starlink satellites, six fitted with cameras to monitor Starship's heat shield.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab lands up to $300M across two new missions, three launches
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab secured contracts covering two missions and three launches worth up to $300 million, adding to its launch backlog even as its stock slides in July amid its pending Iridium acquisition.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 13 launches successfully, deploys first operational Starlink V3 satellites; booster has hard splashdown
story_updates.summary: SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 became the first Starship mission to deploy operational satellites, releasing 20 next-generation Starlink V3 satellites in suborbit that made contact with ground receivers before burning up as planned. The Ship also re-lit an engine in space and made a soft splashdown in the Indian Ocean. Booster 20 struggled on its landing burn attempt, with only 10 of its Raptor engines relighting and two shutting off early, resulting in a hard splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab to open a fourth launch site at Kodiak, Alaska under a $266M Space Force deal
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab will build a new launch site at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Kodiak, Alaska under a $266 million U.S. Space Force contract covering 12 suborbital missile-defence missions with options for six more, first launch no earlier than end of 2026. Flights are expected to use HASTE, the suborbital Electron variant for hypersonic testing. It becomes Rocket Lab's fourth launch site alongside LC-1 in New Zealand and LC-2/LC-3 in Virginia, and reflects the Space Force looking to ease pressure on Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg.

story_updates.headline: Space Force picks Rocket Lab for suborbital launches from the Alaska spaceport
story_updates.summary: Air & Space Forces Magazine on the same award, framed from the service side: the Space Force is spreading launch demand beyond its two busiest ranges, with Kodiak's high-latitude, wide-azimuth corridor suited to missile-defence and high-inclination national security missions.

story_updates.headline: Elon Musk’s Wealth Sinks Below $700 Billion As SpaceX Rout Extends
story_updates.summary: A further decline in SpaceX shares on Monday cut Elon Musk’s net worth by more than $20 billion, lowering his fortune below the $700 billion threshold for the first time since December, as Musk falls further from his trillionaire status. Read the full story on Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2026/07/27/elon-musks-wealth-sinks-below-700-billion-as-spacex-rout-extends/ Subscribe to F

story_updates.headline: SpaceX wins $1.6B US Space Force order for 18 Falcon 9 launches
story_updates.summary: SpaceX won $1.6 billion in orders from the U.S. Space Force to launch 18 Falcon 9 missions through 2027 carrying Pentagon satellites for detecting and targeting airborne objects, flying from Vandenberg Space Force Base as part of the Space Based Sensing and Targeting portfolio supporting the Golden Dome missile defense shield.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab stock jumps on new multi-launch Electron agreement with Japan's iQPS
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab shares jumped over 8% after the company disclosed a new multi-launch agreement with Japanese satellite firm iQPS (Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space), securing three additional dedicated Electron launches, even as the stock remains well off its late-May peak.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX posts first earnings as a public company; Starlink tops 12M subscribers ahead of $120B insider lockup unlock
story_updates.summary: SpaceX released its first quarterly (Q2 2026) earnings report as a public company after markets closed Aug. 4, with shares up about 6% at the open despite trading more than 50% below its post-IPO high. Starlink subscriber count surpassed 12 million and was the company's only profitable business last year, generating $4.42 billion in income. The earnings date also triggers the first tranche of a staggered insider share unlock beginning Aug. 6, potentially freeing up to 911.5 million shares (roughly $120B) held by early investors and employees; Elon Musk's own ~6.4 billion-share stake remains under a separate 366-day lockup.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX targets next Starship test flight this month, aims to land upper stage for first time
story_updates.summary: Elon Musk said on SpaceX's first earnings call since its IPO that the next Starship flight, tentatively scheduled for late August, will send upgraded Starlink satellites to orbit and attempt to land the upper stage rather than splash it down, a major step up from July's ocean landing test.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX rocket expected to have crashed into Moon in unintentional collision

story_updates.summary: Part of a SpaceX rocket hurtling towards the Moon is thought to have made impact. The Falcon 9 rocket was launched last year - its 4,000kg upper stage was shed in space, as planned, but went on to be in an accidental collision course with the lunar surface. story_updates.summary: SpaceX’s stock once again took a hit on Wednesday after the rocket maker posted its first-ever earnings report, which seemingly spooked investors and analysts after the Elon Musk-led firm announced a sixfold increase in quarterly spending. Read the full story on Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2026/08/05/spacex-shares-plunge-13-as-elon-musks-fortune-sheds-80-billion-heres-what-anal

story_updates.headline: Space Force bets $397M on Rocket Lab's Neutron for airborne threat tracking
story_updates.summary: The U.S. Space Force awarded Rocket Lab a $397 million contract to design, build, launch and operate a fleet of 'Flatellite' spacecraft for the Space-Based Airborne Moving Target Indicator program, naming Neutron as the launch vehicle for the first time — the rocket's first publicly confirmed national security mission ahead of its planned Q4 2026 debut.

story_updates.headline: Blue Origin traces New Glenn explosion to engine oxygen valve, targets return to flight this year
story_updates.summary: Blue Origin said the May pad explosion that destroyed a New Glenn booster and damaged Launch Complex-36 originated at the main oxygen valve on one of the rocket's seven BE-4 engines. The company is retrofitting existing engines with small valve modifications, expects updated hardware by end of August, and is targeting a return to flight before the end of 2026; it has also partnered with NASA to test New Glenn hardware at Stennis Space Center this fall.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab posts record Q2 revenue, unveils GHOST launch system and Kepler Neutron mission
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab reported record Q2 2026 revenue of $234 million (up 62% YoY) and a record $2.36 billion backlog, guiding to another record quarter in Q3. The company also unveiled GHOST, a globally-deployable containerized launch system, was selected to launch a dedicated Neutron mission for Kepler Communications, and formally established Rocket Lab Germany GmbH.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab establishes German subsidiary, unveils GHOST containerized mobile launch system
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab announced the creation of Rocket Lab Germany, headquartered in Munich, building on its 2025 acquisition of laser-comms maker Mynaric. Separately the company unveiled GHOST (Global Hypersonic & Orbital Spaceport Technology), a containerized deployable launch system packaging Electron/HASTE rockets and ground support into standard shipping containers for rapid global deployment; its first permanent site will be Launch Complex 4 at the Pacific Spaceport Complex in Kodiak, Alaska, with a suborbital demo flight targeted for 2027.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX sets company record with two Falcon 9 launches 38.5 minutes apart, carrying Globalstar and classified Space Force payloads
story_updates.summary: SpaceX launched back-to-back Falcon 9 missions from Cape Canaveral and Vandenberg just 38.5 minutes apart, a new company record beating its prior mark by 27 minutes. The first carried eight Globalstar satellites, the second a classified USSF-366 payload; the booster's landing was SpaceX's 650th successful Falcon recovery.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab-built satellite platforms for MDA Space/Globalstar successfully reach orbit
story_updates.summary: The first eight of 17 Rocket Lab-built spacecraft buses under a $143M MDA Space contract reached orbit after launching Aug. 15 on a SpaceX Falcon 9, with Rocket Lab confirming all eight are performing nominally and generating power as they begin commissioning to extend Globalstar's direct-to-device network.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab onboarded to $981M Space Force NITE-STAR test-and-training contract
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab was added to the U.S. Space Force's NITE-STAR (Space Test and Range) IDIQ contract with a $981M ceiling, alongside other defense contractors, allowing it to compete for individual task orders spanning satellite development, space software, ground systems and sustainment.

story_updates.headline: Space Force selects Rocket Lab for Space Data Network Consortium, awards $12M in optical comms contracts
story_updates.summary: The U.S. Space Force's Space Systems Command onboarded Rocket Lab to the Space Data Network Consortium, competitively awarding two delivery orders worth $12 million to demonstrate secure optical satellite communications for the Space Data Network Backbone program. Rocket Lab plans a live space demonstration in 2027 using its Photon spacecraft with optical hardware, extending the company's push into military space communications infrastructure.

story_updates.headline: Musk backs off catch-attempt plan for next Starship flight, launch slips toward September
story_updates.summary: Elon Musk indicated in a social media post that SpaceX will probably not attempt to catch the Starship upper stage on its next flight as earlier promised at the Aug. 4 earnings call, saying the tower catch will likely happen 'in a few months' instead. The next Starship flight, expected to be the vehicle's first mission to an operational orbit deploying Starlink satellites, is now sliding into September.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX Announces ‘Biggest Launch Site On Earth’ In Louisiana—Here’s What We Know
story_updates.summary: SpaceX on Tuesday announced plans to build a Starship launch site in southern Louisiana that CEO Elon Musk claimed will be the “biggest launch site on Earth,” expanding the rocket maker’s operations with a $100 billion investment. Read the full story on Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/sites/tylerroush/2026/08/25/spacex-announces-biggest-launch-site-on-earth-in-louisiana-heres-what-we-know/ Subscrib

story_updates.summary: Stoke Space has set out a two-rocket plan: Nova Pathfinder, targeted for a first flight in 2027, and Nova Block 2, a fully reusable 15-tonne vehicle aimed at 2029. story_updates.summary: BBC live coverage of SpaceX's Starship attempting its first orbital flight, a roughly 10-hour mission planned to make about six orbits of the Earth.

story_updates.headline: Live: Unprecedented test flight of SpaceX’s Starship will aim for orbit
story_updates.summary: The most powerful rocket ever made, SpaceX’s Starship, is set to make a massive leap forward in its testing campaign. It will seek to reach orbit for the first time and deploy operational Starlink internet satellites. Watch 24/7 live news with CNN Headlines: https://bit.ly/4eIvlTr #News #space #spacex

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab pushes Neutron's first flight to 2027 after voids found in first-stage tank dome; shares fall ~11%
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab's Oct 14 Neutron development update moved the rocket's debut from late 2026 into 2027 after inspections found voids in the carbon-composite dome of the first-stage propellant tank. CEO Peter Beck outlined a three-step plan targeting Q1 2027 completion, with a firm date to follow. Shares fell about 11% on the news.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX flies its 700th Falcon 9 on a Halloween-eve Starlink launch from Vandenberg, its 11th orbital flight of October
story_updates.summary: SpaceX closed out October with a Starlink launch from Vandenberg, the 700th Falcon 9 flight; the booster landed on the droneship. Spaceflight Now notes SpaceX is beginning to wind down Falcon as it shifts focus to Starship.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab launches Japanese iQPS radar satellite on Electron, its 99th mission to date
story_updates.summary: An Electron rocket lifted off from Rocket Lab's New Zealand site carrying an iQPS Earth-observing radar satellite — the company's 99th mission overall and its 17th Electron flight of the year.

story_updates.headline: Blue Origin pushes New Glenn's return to flight to January 2027 as it rebuilds the launchpad damaged in May explosion
story_updates.summary: Blue Origin told staff the next New Glenn launch now targets early 2027, roughly 10 days later than its previous target, as repairs continue on the pad damaged in a May explosion.

story_updates.headline: SpaceX's Starship Flight 15 slips a day to no earlier than November 13 after full-duration six-engine static fire
story_updates.summary: The next integrated Starship test flight is now targeted for November 13 at the earliest; the ship assigned to Flight 15 completed a full-duration static fire of all six engines.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 15, SpaceX's first attempt to catch both booster and ship, awaits an FAA licence modification ahead of a Nov 13 target
story_updates.summary: Booster 22 and Ship 42 have completed full-duration static fires and are in final processing for a no-earlier-than 13 November launch carrying 26 Starlink satellites. The dual-catch profile, including returning the ship to the Starbase tower, still needs the FAA to approve a licence modification; Musk put the ship-catch odds at 'more likely than not'.

story_updates.headline: Rocket Lab posts record $267.8M Q3 revenue and books $515M+ of Neutron launches, but Neutron's debut stays in 2027
story_updates.summary: Rocket Lab's Q3 2026 results showed record revenue of $267.8M and a $3.57B backlog. It signed eight Neutron missions with five constellation operators worth more than $515M, taking the Neutron backlog to 16 missions, and raised the base price to $70M from $55M. Neutron's first flight remains slipped to 2027 after voids were found in the stage-1 tank dome.

story_updates.headline: Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital offers Rocket Lab a $150M conditional loan to speed up Neutron
story_updates.summary: The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Rocket Lab USA to support Neutron's flight rate once the rocket begins flying. No closing date was given.

story_updates.headline: Launch day for Starship Flight 15: SpaceX targets a 75-minute window for its first attempt to catch both booster and ship
story_updates.summary: SpaceX is targeting a 75-minute window opening at 5:45 p.m. ET (22:45 UTC) on Nov. 13 from Starbase for Flight 15, with Booster 22 and Ship 42 both due to return to the launch site for tower catches — which would be the first full recovery of an orbital launch system. Pre-launch reports said no FAA approval of the required licence modification had been announced as of Thursday.

story_updates.headline: Starship Flight 15 reaches orbit and deploys Starlink satellites, but SpaceX aborts the booster catch and Super Heavy diverts offshore
story_updates.summary: SpaceX launched its 15th Starship from Pad 2 at Starbase on Nov 13. The ship reached orbit about 27 minutes after liftoff and began releasing 26 Starlink satellites. The planned first-ever booster catch at the new pad was aborted, and the booster diverted to an offshore splashdown, so the first attempt to recover both stages fell short.

story_updates.summary: Russia's new Geran/Shahed variants use machine-vision AI to recognize and track ground targets in the terminal phase, while Ukraine fields autonomous interceptor drones that lock onto and destroy Shaheds with minimal human input.

story_updates.headline: NATO commits $40B to counter-drone systems as Germany funds 50,000 AI drones for Ukraine
story_updates.summary: NATO allies announced over $40 billion for counter-drone capabilities and expanded drone-operator training under a new Drone Edge Initiative. Germany separately backed a 90-million-euro contract to supply 50,000 AI-enabled FPV drones to Ukraine, part of a broader $49 billion month of European drone-warfare investment that also included a UK program committing to weapons that make targeting decisions without per-strike human authorization and a $1.8 billion raise for defense-AI startup Helsing.

story_updates.summary: After combat trials intercepting jet-powered Shahed drones, SkyFall unveiled the AI-guided P1-SUN JetKiller; serial production is slated for August 2026 at up to 50,000 interceptors a month.

story_updates.headline: US Marine Corps turns to AI-powered Bullfrog as drone threats expand
story_updates.summary: The Marine Corps selected Allen Control Systems' Bullfrog, an AI-enabled weapon system that detects, tracks and automatically aims firearms at aerial drone threats, for integration into its airborne defenses.

story_updates.headline: UFORCE and ReconCraft to build Ukraine's Magura naval drones in the US
story_updates.summary: British-Ukrainian defense-tech firm UFORCE signed a teaming agreement with Oregon boat-builder ReconCraft to manufacture the combat-proven Magura USV — which has sunk more than a dozen Russian warships and downed manned aircraft — on US soil, with production planned in Oregon and South Carolina scaling toward thousands of units annually.

story_updates.headline: Why Europe is betting big on drones
story_updates.summary: Governments are leaning into drone technology — and fast. Battlefield lessons from Ukraine are reshaping procurement decisions across Europe. It's creating opportunities not only for drone manufacturers but also for companies developing AI, software, electronic warfare, and secure communications.

story_updates.headline: US Senate panel approves AI and autonomous weapons rules amid Pentagon policy shift
story_updates.summary: A Senate committee advanced draft legislation to regulate autonomous weapons systems and military AI, reflecting growing unease in Congress over the administration's revisions to Pentagon AI policy.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine carries out aerial assaults dropping robots from drones
story_updates.summary: Ukraine for the first time employed 'marsupial' drone tactics in combat, using a heavy-lift drone to deploy an ARK-1 ground robot carrying an anti-tank mine behind enemy lines, showcasing long-range, low-risk deployment by teaming uncrewed aerial and ground systems.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine's battlefield AI now spots 70% of enemy targets across 100,000 monthly drone video streams
story_updates.summary: Ukrainian battlefield-AI systems are now flagging roughly 70% of enemy targets across 100,000 drone video streams processed monthly, part of a broader summer 2026 shift toward automated target recognition as Ukraine opens its Avengers Labs AI training platform to domestic defense firms.

story_updates.headline: AI-powered Auterion drone swarms head to European battlefields
story_updates.summary: Auterion's AI-enabled autonomous drone swarm technology is being fielded for European battlefields, with at least six European defense firms having tested swarm control allowing one operator to run 18 drones simultaneously, part of a broader push toward mass-produced autonomous weapons.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine strikes Wildberries site in Moscow #Ukraine #Russia #Wildberries
story_updates.summary: Video from the Moscow region shows plumes of smoke rising from the site of a Wildberries warehouse following an attack by Ukrainian drones on Sunday. Officials said an 83-year-old man had been killed with several others injured in the strikes. story_updates.headline: Fully autonomous AI drone swarm reportedly kills Russian soldiers without human oversight
story_updates.summary: Small Wars Journal reports a swarm of 10 Ukrainian drones cut communications links, used onboard AI to search for and strike targets, and killed without human input in the final attack decision — if confirmed, the first publicly reported use of fully autonomous lethal systems against human targets in combat.

story_updates.headline: NYT: forensic teardown shows Russian drone picked its own target via onboard Nvidia chip, killing 3 civilians in Zaporizhzhia
story_updates.summary: The New York Times reported that a Russian Molniya attack drone recovered by Ukraine after a July 6 strike on a Zaporizhzhia gas station had no communications antenna and instead ran an Nvidia Jetson Orin minicomputer that selected its target autonomously. The unencrypted module let investigators view the terrain imagery and target classes it had been trained to recognise, most likely the propane tanks it struck. Three civilians were killed, in what analysts call one of the first documented fully autonomous drone kills.

story_updates.headline: UN chief and Red Cross renew joint call for a binding treaty on lethal autonomous weapons
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres and the ICRC president issued a joint warning that the world is 'dangerously close to crossing a moral red line: the autonomous targeting of humans by machines,' urging states to negotiate a legally binding agreement banning unpredictable autonomous weapons and those that target people without human control ahead of the November Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons review conference. The appeal followed unconfirmed battlefield reports of fully autonomous, AI-guided drones being used to kill.

story_updates.headline: Hegseth sets up new command to speed drone and AI warfare; Congress adds human-oversight rules for AI weapons
story_updates.summary: NPR reports the Pentagon is forging ahead on autonomous weaponry, with Defense Secretary Hegseth announcing a new military command to accelerate drone and AI adoption under his 'AI-first' directive, while lawmakers added provisions to the annual defense bill requiring human oversight of AI-controlled weapons.

story_updates.headline: Ukrainian ground robot completes first combat-zone logistics mission under AI control
story_updates.summary: Ukrainian officials say an unmanned ground vehicle drove nearly all of a 20-km logistics route autonomously under AI control, described as the first such use in combat conditions. Separately, NPR reports dozens of Ukrainian units now field the autonomous Lupynis-10-TFL-1 drone while Russia deploys its own AI-enabled drones. Claims are from Ukrainian military officials.

story_updates.headline: Kim Jong Un urges drone dominance, calls high-level AI in unmanned weapons a top military priority for North Korea
story_updates.summary: After a weapons display of drones and missiles, North Korean leader Kim Jong Un pressed for faster drone and AI development, saying the use of high-level artificial intelligence in unmanned weapons systems should be a top priority, KCNA reported. South Korea's military said the North had fired around 10 projectiles, including short-range ballistic missiles, amid border tensions.

story_updates.headline: Australia unveils Ghost Shark underwater drone payloads, including sea mines and Altius-600 loitering-munition swarms
story_updates.summary: The Royal Australian Navy revealed payload types for its Anduril-built Ghost Shark extra-large autonomous underwater vehicles, including sea mines and a swarm of Altius-600 loitering munitions, as part of an A$1.7bn fleet programme.

story_updates.headline: Senior Pentagon official says Ukraine's drone war caught the US by surprise; DIU 'starting from basically zero' on cheap drones
story_updates.summary: Under Secretary Emil Michael said the US was caught off guard by drone combat in Ukraine and is working to equip the Army with autonomous systems for Europe and the Middle East; acting DIU director Travis Metz said the department is starting from basically zero on manufacturing cheap expendable drones.

story_updates.headline: Shield AI to acquire radar maker Echodyne to build out its counter-drone business
story_updates.summary: The autonomy firm behind the Hivemind pilot and X-BAT fighter drone is buying Echodyne, whose radars are used to detect small drones.

story_updates.headline: Pentagon gives robotics startup Machina Labs $9M to build airframes for its cheap LUCAS one-way attack drones
story_updates.summary: An 18-month trial contract has Machina Labs producing metal airframes for the Low-Cost Uncrewed Combat Attack System (LUCAS), part of the Pentagon's push for mass-produced, inexpensive attack drones.

story_updates.headline: Facing jet-drone swarms, Ukraine shifts air defence to AI-assisted turrets and interceptor drones using less ammunition
story_updates.summary: Ukrainian defenders are scaling up domestic production of interceptor drones and AI-assisted weapons against Russia's jet-powered drone swarms. One operator can run three gun turrets, with AI tracking incoming drones and correcting aim.

story_updates.headline: Shield AI's Hivemind flies US Air Force drones through coordinated air-combat manoeuvres for the first time
story_updates.summary: Shield AI said its Hivemind autonomy software let multiple Air Force combat drones fly coordinated air-to-air manoeuvres in October demonstrations; weapons-release authority remained with human operators.

story_updates.headline: PLA report outlines China's shift to AI-powered drone warfare, including mass mobilisation of civilian drones
story_updates.summary: A PLA report described plans for AI-enabled drone warfare including strikes on enemy commanders and civilian drone mobilisation; analysts argue Party control requirements over AI drones may slow Chinese kill chains.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani unveils 30% discount on groceries, meat and pantry staples at new municipal stores
story_updates.summary: Mayor Mamdani announced that a core basket of everyday groceries, including all fresh produce, meat and seafood plus roughly 20 pantry categories, will be 30% cheaper at the five new municipal grocery stores regardless of customer income, drawing criticism from commentators who called the pricing unsustainable.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani announces "OPEN for Small Business": over 50 reforms to cut red tape
story_updates.summary: Mayor Mamdani unveiled a package of more than 50 regulatory reforms aimed at reducing paperwork and bureaucratic burden for the city's roughly 180,000 small businesses.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani won't rule out cash reparations, awaits NYC commission findings
story_updates.summary: Mayor Mamdani said he supports continued study of reparations for slavery in New York City and won't rule out cash payments if the city's Commission on Racial Equity recommends them next summer, standing by past statements that New York was complicit in the slave trade.

story_updates.headline: Confusion reigns among NYC homeowners over eligibility for Mamdani's new pied-à-terre tax
story_updates.summary: Nearly a week after city tax officials released information on who could be on the hook for the new pied-à-terre tax on second homes worth over $5 million, attorneys and homeowners say they are baffled by the process overseen by Mayor Mamdani's administration. A City Hall official clarified that letters were sent to roughly 17,000 addresses suspected of being second homes.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani and Finance Commissioner extend pied-a-terre tax exemption deadline after confusing rollout
story_updates.summary: Following confusion after the Department of Finance posted a database of 900,000+ properties that "may" be subject to the new non-primary-residence surcharge (city says only ~17,000 addresses worth over $5M actually got notice letters), Mayor Mamdani and Commissioner Richard Lee announced a four-week extension, giving homeowners until Sept. 18, 2026 (from Aug. 21) to file exemption appeals.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani's Rent Freeze Heaps Pressure on a Teetering CMBS Deal
story_updates.summary: A $506 million commercial mortgage-backed securities deal tied to New York rent-stabilized apartments was already souring for bond investors, and Mayor Mamdani's citywide rent freeze on stabilized units threatens to worsen the outlook for the bundled loan.

story_updates.headline: Mayor Mamdani breaks ground on NYC affordable housing project
story_updates.summary: NYC Mayor Mamdani broke ground on an affordable housing project, per an August 3 announcement from the Mayor's Office.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani dismisses entire business advisory board of NYC's Mayor's Fund
story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani dismissed the business and civic leaders who advised the Mayor's Fund to Advance New York City, the multimillion-dollar philanthropic arm that channels private donations into public programs. The city said the entire board of advisers was disbanded, thanking members for their service; it marks the first time in at least three mayoral administrations that all members of the advisory group were dismissed at once.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani's office denies ID will be required to shop at city-owned grocery stores after backlash
story_updates.summary: After a clip of an NYCEDC official discussing a possible loyalty-card system for the city's planned municipal grocery stores went viral, Trump and allies accused Mamdani of hypocrisy given his opposition to voter ID laws. City Hall clarified the stores will be open to all with no ID, residency or income verification required; a card akin to a supermarket loyalty card is still under discussion to manage supply.

story_updates.headline: Bus fare evasion rises in New York as riders wait for Mamdani's free-ride promise
story_updates.summary: Nearly half of NYC bus riders skipped paying the fare this year through June per MTA data, with fare revenue down $31 million during Mamdani's first six months in office, as his campaign promise of fare-free buses remains unrealized and Albany calls the plan not financially feasible this year.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani sends cease-and-desist letters to Target, Amazon over illegal e-bike and scooter sales
story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani sent cease-and-desist letters to about 40 major retailers, including Target and Amazon, demanding they stop selling prohibited motorized scooters and e-bikes to New York City residents and businesses. Stores face fines of up to $2,000 per sale starting August 18 as part of a broader city crackdown.

story_updates.headline: DOJ sends Mamdani letter seeking answers on alleged unequal treatment of Jewish New Yorkers
story_updates.summary: The Justice Department's Civil Rights Division, led by Assistant AG Harmeet Dhillon, sent Mayor Mamdani a letter requesting a response to allegations of 'unequal treatment' of Jewish residents, following complaints from former state assemblyman Dov Hikind and after recent antisemitic stabbing attacks on the Upper West Side.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani faces questions over ties to antisemitic outlet Uncivilized Media
story_updates.summary: NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani is facing scrutiny after Fox News Digital found he was still following Uncivilized Media, a Qatar-based outlet the ADL says promotes antisemitic conspiracy tropes, on Instagram as of July 24, 2026; the ADL suggested Mamdani could address concerns by publicly condemning the outlet.

story_updates.headline: NYPD refuses security detail for Mamdani's wife's Syria-Lebanon trip
story_updates.summary: City Hall initially said an NYPD detail had been arranged for First Lady Rama Duwaji's planned September trip to Syria and Lebanon, both under State Department 'Do Not Travel' advisories. The NYPD pushed back, saying officers do not accompany civilians to level-four-advisory countries for non-investigative reasons; Mayor Mamdani later confirmed his wife would travel without an NYPD detail.

story_updates.headline: Appellate judge lifts block on Mamdani's pied-à-terre tax, rollout to resume
story_updates.summary: After a Staten Island judge temporarily blocked the rollout of Mamdani's surcharge on second homes worth over $5 million pending an appeal, an appellate judge lifted that block, letting the city resume implementation while the legal fight continues. Oral arguments are set for Aug. 31.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani offers new details on plan for five city-owned grocery stores
story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani provided additional specifics on his proposal to open five government-owned supermarkets in New York City, reviving comparisons to Soviet-era shortages from critics while framing it as a cost-of-living measure.

story_updates.headline: Some 9/11 families publicly defend Mamdani's inclusion in 25th-anniversary ceremony after exclusion petition
story_updates.summary: After a petition backed by ~60,000-77,000 signatures (and endorsed by GOP senators) urged organizers to exclude Mayor Mamdani from the 25th-anniversary Sept. 11 commemoration, the group September 11th Families for Peaceful Tomorrows publicly defended his inclusion, condemning what it called 'anti-American accusations and Islamophobic sentiment' behind the exclusion push. Mamdani has said he will attend.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani sues to block $10,000 teaching aide bonuses passed by City Council
story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani filed a lawsuit challenging a new law granting NYC teaching aides a one-time $10,000 bonus, after the City Council secured enough votes to override his veto.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani unveils $4 billion, 10-year plan to rehabilitate city-owned BQE Central
story_updates.summary: Returning from a weeklong vacation, Mayor Zohran Mamdani and the city's transit chief announced a roughly $4 billion, decade-long rehabilitation of the city-owned Brooklyn-Queens Expressway (BQE Central), aiming to extend the aging cantilevered highway's design life by about two decades without closing the Brooklyn Promenade. Construction is set to break ground in 2030.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani launches 15-member Business Advisory Council; Chobani and Etsy CEOs join, Wall Street and Big Tech decline
story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani unveiled a Business Advisory Council of roughly 15 executives that will meet quarterly to advise him and Deputy Mayor for Economic Justice Julie Su. Members include former UBS Americas chief Robert Wolf, Chobani founder Hamdi Ulukaya, Amalgamated Bank CEO Priscilla Sims Brown, Etsy CEO Kruti Patel Goyal, Northwell Health's Dr. John D'Angelo, RXR Realty's Scott Rechler and NY Liberty CEO Keia Clarke. Reports noted major Wall Street banks and large tech firms declined to participate, underscoring continued friction between the business community and the democratic-socialist mayor.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani administration unveils redesign of Brooklyn's deadly Third Avenue, work to start next year
story_updates.summary: At an Oct 28 transportation press conference, Mayor Mamdani announced a street-safety redesign of Brooklyn's Third Avenue, saying he was tired of learning the names of New Yorkers only after preventable crashes. Construction is slated to begin next year, with completion targeted for end of 2028.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani dodges on NYPD's use of Stingray cellphone trackers; administration drops planned no-bid contract with Israeli tech firm
story_updates.summary: Asked whether he backs the NYPD's cellphone-tracking devices, which the department already uses and is procuring more of, Mamdani declined to say. His administration no longer plans a no-bid contract with a controversial Israeli tech company after pushback from allies and advocates.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani says Trump agreed to grant visa to mother of 15-year-old Ghanaian immigrant shot dead in the Bronx
story_updates.summary: After a phone call with President Trump, Mayor Mamdani announced that the mother of Javits Frimpong, a 15-year-old killed in a Bronx shooting, will be granted a visa to attend his funeral. No arrests have been made.

story_updates.summary: Mayor Zohran Mamdani threatened new legal action against ICE over its use of city-owned parking lots and issued a policy directing Parks Department staff to deny ICE agents access to city lots or non-public park areas without a warrant. DHS said ICE's presence is fully authorized under federal law.

story_updates.headline: Voters approve all five of Mamdani's government-efficiency ballot proposals on permitting, contracting and outdoor dining
story_updates.summary: More than a million New Yorkers backed each of the five charter proposals from Mamdani's Commission on Government Efficiency, aimed at speeding outdoor dining approvals, city contracting and permitting; the mayor used the result to push a faster agenda.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani administration starts work on Brooklyn bus and protected bike lanes on Atlantic and DeKalb avenues
story_updates.summary: City crews began bus-lane and protected-bike-lane changes through Fort Greene, Clinton Hill and Bed-Stuy, aiming to speed B38 trips by about 20% — a first concrete step on the mayor's fast-bus agenda after the election.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani reportedly works to build support for a progressive or labour-backed 2028 Democratic presidential candidate
story_updates.summary: Citing an Axios report, Mamdani has held private meetings with union leaders including the AFA's Sara Nelson and plans to meet the UAW's Shawn Fain, seeking influence over the 2028 Democratic presidential primary. He has not endorsed anyone and has not committed to backing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez if she runs.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani mobilises citywide winter response with $25M expanded Code Blue and boosted snow and ice removal
story_updates.summary: The Mayor's Office announced a $25 million investment in an expanded Code Blue system for people experiencing homelessness and a scaled-up snow and ice clearing operation, and addressed whether schools will use snow days or remote learning.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani signs the Community Opportunity to Purchase Act, giving nonprofits first shot at buying multifamily buildings
story_updates.summary: COPA lets qualified nonprofits and community groups buy certain multifamily buildings before they reach the private market, covering roughly 2,100 apartment buildings; critics expect legal challenges.

story_updates.headline: Mamdani completes McGuinness Boulevard redesign in Greenpoint with full-length parking-protected bike lanes
story_updates.summary: Mayor Mamdani and DOT Commissioner Mike Flynn announced the completed redesign of McGuinness Boulevard: parking-protected bike lanes along the whole corridor from Meeker Avenue to the Pulaski Bridge and one travel lane in each direction. The boulevard carries more than 4,000 daily riders in summer; State Sen. Kristen Gonzalez said it previously saw a crash every other day.

story_updates.headline: Trump signs NDAA repealing the Caesar Act, lifting Syria's core sanctions regime
story_updates.summary: Section 6211 of the FY2026 National Defense Authorization Act repeals the 2019 Caesar Syrian Civilian Protection Act outright, with no conditions attached to the Syrian government. The House passed the bill on 10 December and the Senate on 17 December. In place of conditions, the president must report to Congress every six months for four years on Damascus's progress on expelling foreign fighters, protecting minorities and relations with Israel. Assad-era figures, captagon traffickers and ISIS/al-Qaeda-linked persons stay sanctioned, and Syria remains a designated State Sponsor of Terrorism — which still blocks US foreign assistance, defence exports and some dual-use trade.

story_updates.headline: Decree No. 13 recognises Kurdish as a national language and restores stripped citizenship
story_updates.summary: Al-Sharaa signed Decree No. 13 of 2026 on 16 January, declaring Syrians of Kurdish origin an integral part of the Syrian people. Kurdish becomes a national language alongside Arabic and may be taught in schools in Kurdish-majority areas; the discriminatory measures flowing from the 1962 Hasakah census are abolished and full citizenship granted to Kurds previously registered as stateless; Nowruz becomes a paid national holiday. The decree is the political half of the SDF integration bargain — the test is implementation, notably whether Kurdish becomes a medium of instruction or only a couple of elective hours a week.

story_updates.headline: Transitional People's Assembly holds first session, tasked with drafting a constitution
story_updates.summary: Syria's 210-seat transitional parliament convened for the first time on 12 July with 206 members present. Two-thirds were chosen by local committees appointed by an electoral commission that al-Sharaa himself appointed; he directly named the remaining third. Its renewable 30-month mandate covers forming a constitution-drafting committee, approving budgets and legislating. Druze-majority Sweida did not designate representatives after last year's sectarian bloodshed — al-Sharaa appointed two members from the province instead. The process drew criticism for having no direct elections and under-representing women and minorities. UN Deputy Special Envoy Claudio Cordone called the opening a milestone in the transition.

story_updates.headline: Al-Sharaa says Syria is working toward a security agreement with Israel
story_updates.summary: In an Al Jazeera interview, al-Sharaa said multi-country negotiations with Israel are focused on getting Israeli forces out of the buffer zone seized after Assad's fall in 2024, and that a security arrangement could open the way to a comprehensive peace without conceding Syria's claim to the Golan Heights. He said Damascus is trying to enlist a broad group of states to push Israel toward a more balanced policy, is avoiding confrontation, and is not considering any military intervention in Lebanon. The remarks sit alongside his becoming the first Syrian president since 1967 to address the UN General Assembly.

story_updates.summary: Bashar al-Assad has been sentenced to death by a Syrian court. story_updates.headline: Turkiye and Syria sign phosphate and energy deals, tripling power transmission to 800MW
story_updates.summary: Turkish and Syrian ministers signed a phosphate memorandum in Damascus and agreed infrastructure due within weeks that will roughly triple cross-border electricity transmission capacity to more than 800 megawatts. Turkey's state oil company TPAO and private Turkish firms signed energy agreements clearing exploration across Syrian onshore and offshore blocks — among the most concrete foreign energy commitments since the change of government. Turkey is Damascus's principal economic lifeline, which is also the lever through which Ankara shapes Syrian policy on the Kurdish file.

story_updates.headline: SDF dissolves itself and merges into the Syrian army, ending Kurdish de facto autonomy
story_updates.summary: Mazloum Abdi announced on 25 August that the Syrian Democratic Forces had completed integration and ceased to exist as an independent force, calling it the start of a transition "from the battlefields to the fields of construction". Military units fold into the army under the Defence Ministry and affiliated security forces into the Interior Ministry; Abdi becomes a presidential adviser and Kurdish commanders take senior posts. Unresolved: whether fighters answer to Damascus or to local commands, where they deploy, the status of the YPJ women's units, and guarantees on Kurdish language, education and local policing. Reporting indicates fewer than half of SDF fighters had actually been absorbed.

story_updates.headline: Analysis: SDF integration is a win for al-Sharaa but 'exists largely on paper'
story_updates.summary: Christian Brakel of the Heinrich Boll Foundation's Beirut office tells DW the dissolution is a substantial win for al-Sharaa's drive to concentrate authority in Damascus, but that a unified army is still more true on paper than on the ground: many SDF fighters are not yet absorbed, the mechanics of integration are unclear, and parts of the existing army — implicated in the Sweida and coastal massacres — are not under full central discipline. He notes the outcome is worse for the SDF than the March 2025 deal, follows the US pivot from the SDF toward Damascus under Turkish pressure, and leaves Kurdish cultural and political rights, not autonomy, as the live question — a plausible source of new grievance if the schooling and constitutional guarantees fall short.
