story_updates.summary: Less than a month before the UN climate conference COP31 opens in Antalya, Türkiye, representatives of three successive summit presidencies gathered to address a pressing question: How can the world restore trust in climate action when the consequences of a warming planet are already being felt?

story_updates.headline: COP17: The world has a plan to save nature. Is it working?
story_updates.summary: The UN Secretary-General has called for an end to the “war on nature”. On Monday, governments gathering in Yerevan, Armenia, will have to confront a more practical question: are they doing enough to win the peace and put the world’s biodiversity goals back on track?

story_updates.headline: Flour sacks turned flood barriers: Gaza faces another winter without safe shelter
story_updates.summary: Like many people in the war-ravaged Gaza Strip, Ahmed Al-Omari is preparing for another winter of bitter cold and rain that threatens to cause flooding as families struggle to survive in tattered tents and damaged buildings.

story_updates.headline: Inside the New York ‘time machine’ racing to save a century of sound and film
story_updates.summary: “I tell my kids I work in a time machine,” said Rhony Dostaly. In a basement beneath Lincoln Center, the media preservation engineer rescues moments from the past. “I go back in time, and I grab elements, and I make them available for people today.”

story_updates.headline: Protecting Earth’s fragile biodiversity takes spotlight at Armenia talks
story_updates.summary: Biodiversity losses continue to upend the lives of billions of people whose future prosperity depends on countries taking urgent action to protect our planet, the top UN official leading talks at the UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, said on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: Funding cuts leave half a million without food assistance
story_updates.summary: Funding shortages have forced the World Food Programme (WFP) to slash assistance to hungry families in the Gaza Strip by roughly one third – a move that will affect some 500,000 people as winter approaches, the UN agency announced on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Guterres honours Indonesian troops who paid ‘ultimate sacrifice’
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres paid tribute to Indonesian peacekeepers on Monday, laying a wreath in honour of four who recently lost their lives in Lebanon and offering a robust defence of UN peacekeeping in what he called “testing times for peace”.

story_updates.headline: ‘Season of fear’: Escalating Israeli attacks on West Bank olive farmers, deadly strikes on Gaza
story_updates.summary: Israeli attacks on war-torn Gaza over the weekend killed at least six Palestinians, including children, despite a year-old ceasefire agreement. Meanwhile, in the occupied West Bank, settler violence continued through the ongoing olive harvest, with UN independent experts on Monday urging Israel to protect Palestinian farmers.

story_updates.headline: Haiti: Elections on hold as gangs adapt to security crackdown, Security Council hears
story_updates.summary: Armed groups in Haiti are adapting to intensified security operations, stepping up reprisals against civilians and extending their reach into rural areas, the UN warned the Security Council on Monday.

story_updates.headline: Hunger is ‘an avoidable tragedy’ in a world of plenty: Türk
story_updates.summary: More than a quarter of humanity struggles to get enough food, even though the world produces enough for everyone, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said on Monday, blaming injustice and the denial of human rights for hunger in a world of plenty.

story_updates.headline: UN condemns deadly wave of drone strikes in war-torn Sudan
story_updates.summary: Drone strikes killed and injured dozens across Sudan on Monday as the ongoing war continues to cause soaring displacement and hunger.

story_updates.headline: Yemen war continues to force families from homes amid hunger and disease
story_updates.summary: More than 250,000 people have now fled renewed fighting in Yemen, the UN said on Tuesday, citing particular concern for those sheltering in the southwestern city of Taiz and the wider governorate, where access is “essentially blocked”.

story_updates.headline: ‘One step away from famine’: Inside Afghanistan’s hunger crisis
story_updates.summary: Following extreme hunger warnings, a bitter reality is unfolding across Afghanistan: food is available, but remains inaccessible for millions of people.

story_updates.headline: Bangladesh: UNICEF chief calls for an end to child marriage
story_updates.summary: At 14, Bushra faced being married off – until community leaders at a UNICEF-supported child protection hub worked with her father to prevent her from being given away against her will.

story_updates.headline: Sudan conflict: Peace efforts resume to end ‘drone war’ fuelling humanitarian crisis
story_updates.summary: Talks to halt the fighting in Sudan and alleviate the humanitarian crisis there continued in Geneva on Wednesday, where nearly two dozen countries convened to discuss a pathway to a ceasefire and transition to peaceful governance that represents all Sudanese people.

story_updates.headline: Summit in Samarkand, a boon for child wellbeing and health
story_updates.summary: Representatives from across the international community are meeting in Samarkand, Uzbekistan, to ensure that children everywhere can thrive in a world marred by war, climate chaos and other fundamental challenges.

story_updates.headline: Fate unknown of many returned to DPR Korea from China: UN independent experts
story_updates.summary: Three years on from the reported resumption of large-scale forcible returns of nationals of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) from China, serious concerns persist about their fate, according to a group of Human Rights Council-appointed independent experts.

story_updates.headline: ‘Connect the dots’ between street protests and global turmoil, urges Guterres
story_updates.summary: The international community must combat inequality and stop wars from expanding to ensure a safer world for all, the UN Secretary-General said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Russian attacks intensify, UN team tours West Bank, ‘unlawful’ elderly deaths
story_updates.summary: Long-range Russian attacks across Ukraine are intensifying, including in Kyiv, causing at least 14 civilian deaths and 78 injuries overnight into Thursday, as UN agencies continue to provide aid.

story_updates.headline: Yemen: Deepening concerns for Taiz City as aid is blocked from entering
story_updates.summary: Aid agencies warned on Friday of the fast-developing humanitarian emergency inside Taiz City in Yemen, which has been encircled by de facto Houthi forces fighting government troops along the country’s west coast.

story_updates.headline: West Bank: Guterres alarmed as Israel imposes sweeping closures after deadly Hebron attack
story_updates.summary: The UN said on Friday it was “extremely alarmed” by intensifying violence in the occupied West Bank, as Israel moved to seal off the territory following a deadly attack on its soldiers in Hebron.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Iran nuclear inspections, deadly church attack in Jordan, El Fasher – one year on
story_updates.summary: The head of the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), Rafael Grossi, called on Friday for a swift return of inspectors to Iran, warning of growing fragility in the global nuclear non-proliferation regime.

story_updates.headline: UN marks 81 years of global cooperation
story_updates.summary: The United Nations celebrates its 81st anniversary on Saturday, highlighting more than eight decades of work to advance peace, human rights and development around the world.

story_updates.headline: Ebola: UN officials condemn killing of nurse in DR Congo
story_updates.summary: The UN’s Ebola coordinator and the head of the World Health Organization (WHO) have deplored the killing of a nurse working to halt the spread of the disease in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

story_updates.headline: In Egypt, Guterres warns against Iran-US escalation
story_updates.summary: UN Secretary-General António Guterres called for dialogue and diplomacy to end the war between Iran and the United States in remarks on Monday to journalists in Cairo, Egypt.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Investigators find Russia committed war crimes by targeting civilians
story_updates.summary: Top human rights experts investigating Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine said on Monday that the Russian authorities had committed war crimes and crimes against humanity by attacking civilians and vital energy infrastructure, among other violations of international law.

story_updates.headline: West Bank: Hebron crackdown displaces thousands, Türk warns of ethnic cleansing
story_updates.summary: Israel’s “aggressive operation” in the West Bank city of Hebron raises serious concerns of ethnic cleansing, UN human rights chief Volker Türk warned on Monday, as the number of Palestinians forced from their homes passed 3,000 on the eve of Israeli elections.

story_updates.headline: Women and girls’ share of civilian war deaths doubles since 2021
story_updates.summary: War is growing deadlier for women and girls, who accounted for one in four of the more than 37,000 civilians killed in armed conflict last year – double their share in 2021 – according to major UN report released Monday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Ethiopians flee to Kenya amidst renewed conflict, new head of UN’s food programme, UN mission in Somalia concludes
story_updates.summary: Around 36,600 people have fled into northern Kenya following an uptick in fighting on the Ethiopian side of the border.

story_updates.headline: Ebola: 20 contacts released from quarantine in Kenya, amid vaccine ‘hope’ in DR Congo
story_updates.summary: Twenty people associated with Kenya’s first case of Ebola Bundibugyo virus disease have been reunited with their families after being released from quarantine following completion of a mandatory 21-day monitoring period.

story_updates.headline: Record carbon dioxide levels will impact us for centuries, says UN weather agency
story_updates.summary: Levels of carbon dioxide (CO2) and other major greenhouse gases in the atmosphere caused by burning fossil fuels reached record highs in 2025, locking in more long-term global warming, the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) said on Tuesday.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: ‘No safe place in Ukraine’, IAEA calls for Iran nuclear inspections, Kenya hosts thousands of Ethiopians fleeing…
story_updates.summary: The UN refugee agency (UNHCR) on Tuesday urged continued international support for Ukraine’s population as Russian airstrikes intensify and humanitarian needs grow in advance of another bitterly cold winter.

story_updates.headline: Four in five domestic workers lack formal job protections, UN finds
story_updates.summary: An estimated 66.5 million domestic workers – representing more than four out of five domestic workers worldwide – were informally employed in 2025, a new report by the UN’s labour organisation has found.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Women and girls face greater dangers in war
story_updates.summary: From Gaza to Yemen, women and girls are facing ever greater dangers this year simply surviving in war zones. The Security Council meets Tuesday to debate the best way to improve security for women caught up in conflict.

story_updates.headline: Gaza: Families brace for fourth winter in tents as aid operations remain stymied
story_updates.summary: Families in Gaza are bracing for a fourth winter in tents and makeshift shelters as UN aid operations face mounting obstacles, with transport suspended on Tuesday due to Israel’s closure of the key Kerem Shalom crossing for election day.

story_updates.headline: General Assembly weighs US embargo against Cuba ahead of 34th vote
story_updates.summary: The General Assembly opened its annual debate on the US economic embargo against Cuba on Tuesday. On Wednesday, 28 October, Member States will vote for the 34th time on a resolution calling for it to end.

story_updates.headline: Higher Ground: How New York is raising a park to hold back the sea
story_updates.summary: On 29 October 2012, Hurricane Sandy slammed into New York City, unleashing a devastating storm surge that flooded homes, subways and tunnels, knocked out power and sparked deadly fires.

story_updates.headline: Ocean’s ability to absorb carbon is weakening as climate change intensifies, UN warns
story_updates.summary: The ocean absorbs around 30 per cent of human-caused carbon dioxide (CO₂) emissions and 90 per cent of excess heat trapped by greenhouse gases. But climate change has already reduced its capacity to absorb carbon by approximately six per cent, a new UN report warns ahead of the COP31 climate conference in November.

story_updates.headline: Record heat-related deaths in 2023, WHO-partnered report finds
story_updates.summary: Climate inaction continues to harm and kill people in all countries with a record 710,000 estimated deaths globally from heat in 2023, a UN-partnered report warned on Wednesday. For the first time, more than seven in 10 fatalities were attributable to human-caused climate change.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo: WHO urges sustained efforts as Ebola cases top 10,000
story_updates.summary: As Ebola cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) surpass the 10,000 mark, the World Health Organization (WHO) has underlined the need for continued efforts to contain spread of the disease.

story_updates.headline: Protecting the storytellers: Women journalists on the frontline of conflict
story_updates.summary: As online abuse, gender-based attacks and impunity ramp up the threats to women reporting from crisis zones, journalists and UN leaders are calling for urgent action to protect those who document conflict.

story_updates.headline: Ending conflict is ‘number one thing’ to reduce world hunger, new WFP chief says
story_updates.summary: Reducing conflict is the single most effective way to tackle global hunger, the new head of the UN World Food Programme (WFP), Luke Lindberg, said on Wednesday, noting that conflict drives two thirds of the acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide.

story_updates.headline: UN human rights chief urges better protection of civilians in conflicts
story_updates.summary: Youth-led protests against corruption and inequality in Serbia, Bangladesh, Nepal and Madagascar reflect a growing demand for reinforcing human rights around the world, UN human rights chief Volker Türk said at a press briefing on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid trapped between drones and incarceration
story_updates.summary: Civilians in Sudan’s El Obeid live in constant fear of drone attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) and of a wave of arbitrary arrests by the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF), UN-appointed independent investigators said on Wednesday.

story_updates.headline: Backing for UN call to end Cuba embargo falls to 20-year low
story_updates.summary: The UN General Assembly on Wednesday called for the 34th time for an end to the US economic, commercial and financial embargo on Cuba – but with the weakest backing for the resolution in two decades.

story_updates.headline: Afghanistan opium production jumps fivefold as farmers find ways round Taliban ban
story_updates.summary: Opium production in Afghanistan has risen fivefold in a year. According to a UN survey released on Thursday, it’s the first significant increase since the Taliban banned poppy cultivation in 2022.

story_updates.headline: Security Council LIVE: Can new technology keep the world’s sea lanes safe?
story_updates.summary: Cheap drones, autonomous vessels and cyberattacks are changing the threats to the world’s shipping lanes – and the tools to counter them. At an open debate on Thursday, the Security Council is weighing how emerging technologies could both endanger and protect seafarers, global trade and food and energy supplies.

story_updates.headline: Nature is making a comeback – now restoration funding must quadruple
story_updates.summary: From salmon spawning grounds in Canada to coral reefs in Indonesia, ecosystems around the world are being restored at an unprecedented rate.

story_updates.headline: Russia drone strike on Ukrainian railway station kills 13
story_updates.summary: The UN’s top humanitarian official in Ukraine on Thursday condemned a Russian drone attack on the city of Dnipro that killed at least 13 civilians and injured 10 others at its main railway station.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: 5 children killed in Sudan, Haiti hunger emergency, Yemen war update
story_updates.summary: At least five children were killed and two others injured in a drone attack on a market in Nyala, in Sudan’s South Darfur state, on Monday, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Thursday.

story_updates.headline: AI is changing the way we think. The question is whether we’ll notice in time
story_updates.summary: Artificial intelligence promises to make life easier. With a few keystrokes, it can write emails, summarize reports, generate ideas and answer complex questions in seconds. For many people, it feels like a technological leap on par with the arrival of the internet itself.

story_updates.headline: Myanmar’s illicit economy fuels escalating violence, with civilians bearing the brunt
story_updates.summary: Myanmar’s human rights situation is “catastrophic”, the UN independent expert on the country warned at a press briefing Thursday, as the war spirals with no end in sight.

story_updates.headline: Yemen war makes reaching assistance too dangerous for many
story_updates.summary: More than 280,000 people have now been displaced by fighting in Yemen and many vulnerable people are unable to access lifesaving relief because it is too dangerous to do so, the UN refugee agency (UNHCR) said on Friday.

story_updates.headline: UN rights office warns of deepening displacement ‘nightmare’ in Gaza
story_updates.summary: Israeli forces continue to push Palestinians into ever-smaller areas of the Gaza Strip while destroying civilian infrastructure and attacking displacement sites, the UN human rights office, OHCHR, warned on Friday amid concerns of ethnic cleansing.

story_updates.headline: DR Congo: Hunger deepens for millions amid conflict, Ebola and climate shocks
story_updates.summary: More than 28 million people in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are not getting enough to eat and the number is expected to tick up in the coming months, according to the latest alert from the IPC global food security monitor.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: Oleshky ceasefire offers ‘hope’ for civilians as attacks on aid vehicles continue
story_updates.summary: Each day the ceasefire in Oleshky holds means hope for civilians in the city, the UN’s top humanitarian official said, stressing that those wishing to leave must be able to do so safely and voluntarily.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: 300,000 displaced in Lebanon, Türk ‘deeply concerned’ over Novaya Gazeta closure, $50 million refugee appeal, World…
story_updates.summary: More than 300,000 people displaced since early March remain internally displaced in Lebanon, where the humanitarian crisis is “far from over,” according to the UN’s aid coordination office (OCHA).

story_updates.headline: DPR Korea: Isolation deepens even as the country changes, says UN rights official
story_updates.summary: The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea (DPRK) is building factories and hospitals, rolling out smartphones and mobile banking, and passing new laws at an unprecedented rate. But its people are more cut off from the outside world than at any point in the country’s history.

story_updates.headline: Samarkand: A ‘living museum’ on the Silk Road grapples with a tourism boom
story_updates.summary: As the sun sets over Samarkand’s majestic Registan, its last rays glint across the turquoise mosaics. Dusk settles on the ancient square where great trade routes have crossed for centuries.

story_updates.headline: Somalia looks to the future as the UN's political mission closes
story_updates.summary: “The story of the UN's political engagement in Somalia has been one of persistence, partnership and adaptation,” Raisedon Zenenga, the UN Secretary-General's Deputy Special Representative for Somalia has said, as three decades of UN political missions in the Horn of Africa country comes to an end on 31 October.

story_updates.headline: ‘They deserve to know the truth’: UN rights chief demands probe into staffer’s death in Houthi custody
story_updates.summary: The UN human rights chief on Saturday demanded an independent investigation into the death of a Yemeni colleague held by the Houthis for more than two years, whose family learned of his death only weeks after it happened.

story_updates.headline: Breaking the silence in Mexico’s barracks
story_updates.summary: In Mexico’s armed forces, an order from a superior is meant to be obeyed without question. For many women in uniform, investigative journalist Zorayda Gallegos found, that can include an order to step into an officer’s bedroom.

story_updates.headline: Western Sahara: UN ‘stands ready’ to keep supporting peace efforts as MINURSO mission ends
story_updates.summary: The UN remains committed to supporting a just, lasting and mutually acceptable political solution in Western Sahara that provides for the self-determination of its people, Secretary-General António Guterres said on Sunday, as the UN peacekeeping mission there began to wind down.

story_updates.headline: COP17: Nations chart ‘Yerevan Pathway’ to speed up action for nature
story_updates.summary: At the halfway mark to 2030, countries meeting in Armenia have agreed a roadmap to accelerate action for nature, after a global review found the world off track to meet its biodiversity targets.

story_updates.headline: Six in seven journalist murders go unpunished, UNESCO reports
story_updates.summary: Global impunity for journalist killings has risen for the first time in more than a decade, while the growing use of drones is an emerging threat for reporters in conflict zones, according to the latest report from UN cultural organization UNESCO.

story_updates.headline: Ethiopia: Violence in the north is pushing health system to the brink, WHO chief warns
story_updates.summary: The head of the World Health Organization (WHO) called on Monday for greater protection for civilians caught in conflict in northern Ethiopia following deadly drone strikes this past weekend.

story_updates.headline: Ukraine: WFP provides hot meals to Oleshky evacuees as UN pushes to restore power before winter
story_updates.summary: The UN World Food Programme (WFP) is providing emergency food assistance to more than 400 people who were able to leave the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, during a brief local ceasefire.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: healthcare crisis in Yemen’s Taiz and Afghanistan, Western Sahara mission's phased closure
story_updates.summary: The humanitarian crisis in Yemen is worsening, particularly in the southwestern city of Taiz, which is being encircled by paramilitary Iran-backed Houthi forces.

story_updates.headline: Underscoring Expanding Reach of Information, Fourth Committee Stresses Need for Accuracy, Multilingualism, Smarter Technology in UN…
story_updates.summary: In a world awash with content, the need for accurate and engaging communications from the United Nations has only increased, the Fourth Committee (Special Political and Decolonization) heard as it began its review of questions relating to information.

story_updates.headline: Security Council 10261st & 10262nd Meetings (AM) International Court of Justice Elections
story_updates.summary: The General Assembly and Security Council will meet concurrently today to fill five vacancies on the International Court of Justice, the principal judicial organ of the United Nations.

story_updates.headline: Air raid alerts and attacks on schools: the devastating face of education in Ukraine
story_updates.summary: Ukraine has sustained almost 2,000 attacks on education since the full-scale Russian invasion in 2022, with some 270 this year alone, the UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) said on Tuesday, a day after a strike at a school being used to distribute aid.

story_updates.headline: Gender equality pays off for business – so why are companies pulling back?
story_updates.summary: Gender equality and diversity are good for business – but while increasing numbers of women are reaching top spots in the corporate world, more initiatives are needed to keep momentum going.

story_updates.headline: Haiti gang leader seeks UN talks as El Salvador sends 2,000 troops to hunt for missing soldiers
story_updates.summary: A Haitian gang leader wanted by the United States has asked the UN to mediate, as El Salvador sends more than 2,000 troops into the country to search for four of its soldiers who went missing after a gang ambush.

story_updates.headline: World News in Brief: Children killed in Myanmar strike, new violence flares in Mozambique, an Internet affordability milestone
story_updates.summary: A school in Myanmar has been hit in an airstrike, with three children reported killed and five others injured, according to UN Children’s Fund UNICEF.

story_updates.headline: Married off at 14: In Yemen’s war, women and girls suffer ‘devastating consequences’
story_updates.summary: Safa is 14. Her mother died earlier this year. She has no brothers or sisters. And a few weeks ago, as the crisis took hold, her father married her to an elderly man, afraid that if he were killed in the hostilities, no one would be left to protect her.

story_updates.headline: ‘This is not about politics. This is about people’: UN warns of impact of deadly drone strikes in Sudan
story_updates.summary: Intensifying drone attacks on civilian infrastructure across Sudan are disrupting electricity, water and fuel supplies, putting lives at risk and hampering the delivery of humanitarian aid, the UN’s top official in the country has warned.

story_updates.headline: New Permanent Representative of Finland Presents Credentials
story_updates.summary: The new Permanent Representative of Finland to the United Nations, Janne Taalas, presented his credentials to UN Secretary-General António Guterres today.

story_updates.headline: Activities of Secretary-General in Indonesia, 17-19 October
story_updates.summary: The United Nations Secretary-General, António Guterres, arrived in Jakarta late on Saturday, 17 October, for an official visit.

story_updates.headline: Daily Press Briefing by the Office of the Spokesperson for the Secretary-General
story_updates.summary: In Gaza, UN partners supporting the collection of solid waste warn that only half of their vehicle fleet is operational due to persistent restrictions imposed by Israeli authorities on the entry of necessary materials. As a result, public health risks are increasing as only some of the trash can actually be collected.

story_updates.headline: First Committee Ends 2026 Session amid Divisions over Working Methods, Forwards 70 Draft Proposals to General Assembly
story_updates.summary: The First Committee (Disarmament and International Security) today forwarded 70 draft proposals to the General Assembly for its action, concluding its 2026 session, which was marked by sharp divisions among Member States on substantive issues, as well as debate over how best to balance demands for greater efficiency with efforts to ensure adequate speaking opportunities and due consideration of...

story_updates.headline: General Assembly Elects 5 Members to International Court of Justice after Three Voting Rounds
story_updates.summary: Today the General Assembly, acting alongside but autonomous of the Security Council, voted to fill five soon-to-be-vacant seats on the International Court of Justice, the Organization’s principal judicial organ and one of its six governance structure entities.

story_updates.headline: Fourth Committee Spotlights Danger to Media, Disinformation in Conflict Zones, Lauding UN Global Communications for Persistent Coverage of…
story_updates.summary: Delegates in the Fourth Committee (Special Political and Decolonization) today expressed concern about the weaponization of information and violence against journalists in a world marked by deepening geopolitical divides.

story_updates.headline: Addressing Sixth Committee, International Court of Justice President Highlights Importance of State Engagement
story_updates.summary: The President of the International Court of Justice, addressing the Sixth Committee (Legal) today per annual tradition, detailed how State engagement with the principal judicial organ of the United Nations extends far beyond the Court’s contentious function.

story_updates.headline: Security Council briefed on Abyei and UNISFA by Lacroix and Special Envoy ahead of 15 November mandate expiry
story_updates.summary: The Council's 10266th meeting took up Sudan and South Sudan: Under-Secretary-General Jean-Pierre Lacroix briefed on the Abyei situation and the UN Interim Security Force for Abyei, whose mandate expires 15 November. The same day the Council also heard the Yemen 2140 sanctions committee briefing.

story_updates.headline: Security Council adopts presidential statement directing all States to settle international disputes by peaceful means
story_updates.summary: Under Latvia's November presidency, the Council adopted a presidential statement stressing de-escalation, mediation and cessation of hostilities in line with the UN Charter, and underscoring the International Court of Justice's role where states consent to its jurisdiction. Same day the Council also met on Yemen and on Sudan/South Sudan (Abyei).

story_updates.headline: AP exclusive: departing UN chief Guterres calls COP31 'a moment of truth' in the fight to curb global warming
story_updates.summary: In an interview ahead of the COP31 climate talks in Antalya, Türkiye, Secretary-General Guterres, whose term ends on 31 December, said every country needs to do more now on fossil-fuel phase-down and climate finance.

story_updates.headline: Guterres warns world has entered a 'new age of climate extremes' as leaders gather for COP31 in Antalya
story_updates.summary: As COP31 opened in Antalya, the Secretary-General issued a statement linking a strong El Niño and climate change to a new era of extreme weather and urged leaders to 'get serious' on emissions cuts.

story_updates.headline: Security Council meets on Ukraine as UN warns strikes on the power grid are 'weaponizing winter' ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
story_updates.summary: At its 10267th meeting, ASG Mohamed Yahya told the Council that Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy infrastructure are causing power and water outages for millions, and that humanitarian aid under a winter plan for 2 million+ people cannot replace a grid repeatedly destroyed. Several members condemned the attacks and voiced hope that US-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi yield humanitarian measures; over 900,000 households in Dnipro and Zhytomyr lost power that weekend.

story_updates.headline: Security Council briefed on South Sudan as UNMISS chief warns country is at a 'critical juncture' six weeks before elections
story_updates.summary: SRSG Anita Kiki Gbeho told the Council that South Sudan faces deepening political uncertainty and worsening violence ahead of its first national elections since independence; the briefing was followed by closed consultations.

story_updates.headline: Security Council to meet on the Middle East after Bahrain's urgent request; Europeans push for emergency session on E1 settlement
story_updates.summary: Bahrain requested an urgent Security Council meeting amid Gulf tensions, while Denmark and other European members pressed for an emergency session on Israeli construction in the E1 area of the West Bank.

story_updates.headline: Security Council renews Yemen sanctions for 12 months, adding maritime expertise to the expert panel (resolution 2837)
story_updates.summary: The Security Council adopted resolution 2837 (2026), renewing the Yemen travel-ban and asset-freeze measures for 12 months and extending the Panel of Experts for 13 months, and asked the Secretary-General to expand the Panel to six members with maritime security expertise to address evolving Houthi threats. The UK said the regime keeps pace with evolving threats; Russia argued blame should not rest entirely with Ansar Allah.

story_updates.headline: Security Council unanimously extends MINUSCA to November 2027, cutting the troop ceiling to 12,000 and planning a handover
story_updates.summary: Resolution 2836 (2026) extends the UN stabilization mission in the Central African Republic until 15 November 2027, lowers the military ceiling from 14,046 to 12,000 (plus 2,265 police and 40 corrections officers) and calls for a phased transfer of tasks to national authorities as conditions allow. France warned security gains remain fragile along the Sudan border; the CAR delegate said it does not want a transfer of tasks only on paper.
